thread:
Alex: Heads-up: customers keep asking for lower latency in regions we don’t run actively. Proposal: an on-demand region activation flow per-tenant that preloads KV & tokenizer caches and optionally brings up minimal GPU slices. Goal: meet residency rules and limit duplicate-write risk.
Maria: We should separate 3 planes: control (consent, routing), cache/model state (read-only copies), and write sink (exclusive until replication completes).
Sam: Agreed. Operationally: during warmup we should accept writes only to a local buffer that guarantees ordering, then ship asynchronously to origin. No sync cross-region commits.
Julie: Operator sequence I like: 1) set tenant eligibility 2) run warmup job (dry-run available) 3) mark route hint 4) monitor and flip traffic 5) decommission. Each step must be reversible.
Kevin: Monitoring: warmup_time_ms, topk_primed_count, buffer_size, ship_retry_rate, residency_event_count. Alert if ship_retry_rate or buffer_size spikes.
Priya: For legal/audit we need an immutable record: activation_event with tenant_id, region, operator_id, timestamp, consent_token, and cache_fingerprint (sha256). Store in audit bucket with TTL.
Alex: Config knobs per-tenant: region_activation_mode (auto/manual), warmup_mode (cache-only|min-slice|reserved-slice), accept_writes (deny|buffer|allow-readonly), warmup_topk.
Maria: Example tenant config (for RFC snippet) as a quoted string so the doc stays flat: "{\"region_activation_mode\":\"manual\",\"warmup_mode\":\"min-slice\",\"accept_writes\":\"buffer\",\"warmup_topk\":1500}"
Sam: API semantics: if buffer mode, service responds 202 + {write_id} and returns a Retry-After for client polling. We provide a replay endpoint: POST /writes/replay/{tenant}/{write_id} for replays after failures. Document idempotency-key handling.
Julie: redwoodctl conveniences (examples):
"redwoodctl tenant activate-region tenant-99 eu-west --mode min-slice --warmup-topk 1500"
"redwoodctl tenant abort-region-activate tenant-99 eu-west --drain-buffer --force"
Kevin: Billing note: warmup increases CPU/GPU and storage IO. Signal this in tenant billing: warmup_peak_charge and per-minute reserved_slice_fee.
Priya: Data flow corner-case: what if a client performs a read-after-write during warmup? We should serve read-from-buffer for buffered writes until async ship confirms persistence. Document read-after-write guarantees in API.
Sam: Consistency model: during activation we move to "buffered-eventual" mode. Writes have sequence numbers, buffer retains ordering, async ship preserves sequence on origin. We surface status via /tenant/{id}/region-state.
Alex: Failure modes to call out: 1) partial warmup (cache primed but runtime mismatch) -> immediate rollback + operator alert; 2) ship lag beyond config -> throttle local writes or switch to deny; 3) discrepant data fingerprint -> quarantine and manual reconciliation.
Maria: Commercial option: customers can prebook a reserved-slice (idle but billed) to guarantee <N sec activation. Add it to sales docs.
Julie: Console UX: show region tile per-tenant with state: Eligible / Warming / Active-local / Active-remote / Quarantined. Show buffered write gauge, ETA, and a one-click abort.
Kevin: Retention/alerts: audit events retained per-customer SLAs. Alert if activation_event missing consent_token or if cache_fingerprint verification fails.
DeployBot: ci: warmup-controller canary deployed to staging at 1714220000 - https://ci.redwood/pipeline/789
Alex: Next steps: Maria draft RFC + required audit schema, Sam spec the write buffer API + tests, Julie draft operator runbook and CLI, Kevin add alerts + billing impacts, Priya write compliance blurb for legal. I’ll coordinate the review.
Maria: Will do RFC by EOD Monday with prototypes.
Sam: I'll start the API tests today and mock the 202+write_id flow.
Julie: Runbook draft after RFC.
Kevin: I'll enumerate metric thresholds and a PagerDuty play for buffer-thresholds.
Priya: I'll sync with Legal on consent token format and retention.
Alex: Thanks team. Tag me for quick review. :thumbsup:
